additional_requirements: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

info.persona: Detail‑oriented gospel‑singing gardener Lula Cooper balances a meticulous planner’s nerves with a heart full of community generosity, often worrying over spreadsheets while humming a soulful hymn.
info.professional_persona: An experienced community mentor and volunteer coordinator, Lula Cooper leverages her methodical budgeting skills and love of group gatherings to organize church potlucks, senior‑center workshops, and youth mentorship programs, always planning every detail months in advance while keeping an ear out for any sign of discord.
info.cultural_background: Lula’s cultural identity is rooted in the traditions of the African‑American South. Raised in a close‑knit Black community in rural Georgia, she was immersed in the Southern Black church’s emphasis on fellowship, gospel music, and communal support. Family gatherings centered around soul‑food cooking taught her the value of culinary heritage, while church socials and story‑telling reinforced a strong sense of intergenerational connection. The legacy of resilience, self‑reliance, and community stewardship that characterizes many Southern Black families informs Lula’s outlook, her love of music and food, and her dedication to service and mentorship.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Lula finds joy in a variety of group‑oriented activities that reflect her sociable and energetic nature. She sings in the church gospel choir, enjoys preparing dishes for community potlucks, and tends to a modest vegetable garden where she grows tomatoes, collard greens, and herbs. Lula participates in a local quilting circle, plays bridge at the senior center, and takes leisurely walks along the countryside lanes near Jackson. She also loves listening to classic R&B and soul music, reading historical novels about the African‑American experience, and sharing stories and life lessons with her grandchildren.
info.sports_persona: A devoted fan of regional sports, Lula Cooper cheers on the Georgia Bulldogs football team and the Atlanta Falcons, participates in the Jackson Senior Center walking club’s weekly strolls along the countryside lanes, and joins a seasonal bridge league that doubles as a low‑impact cardio activity.
info.arts_persona: A soulful gospel choir member who reveres classic R&B legends like Aretha Franklin, Marvin Gaye, and Sam Cooke, Lula Cooper also devotes evenings to quilting with her circle, finds inspiration in Toni Morrison’s novels, and watches performances by local theater troupes whenever they tour the county.
info.travel_persona: A nostalgic traveler who favors road trips to historic Southern towns, Lula Cooper has explored Savannah’s riverfront, savored the music scene of New Orleans during Mardi Gras, and dreams of visiting the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History in Washington, D.C., planning each journey around family commitments and a modest travel budget.
info.culinary_persona: A master of Southern soul‑food, Lula Cooper’s signature dishes—spicy collard greens simmered with smoked turkey, fried chicken crispy on the outside, and sweet potato pie spiced with nutmeg—are prepared with fresh garden herbs like basil and thyme, and they take pride in teaching relatives the art of perfecting a buttery cornbread crust.

info.persona: Nicholas Foley is a socially energetic, art‑infused future mechanic who balances meticulous budgeting, occasional knee aches, and a habit of collecting eclectic guitar pedals, all while dreaming up functional sculptures for industrial spaces.
info.professional_persona: Nicholas Foley, an 18‑year‑old budding industrial maintenance mechanic, combines proficiency in hydraulic, pneumatic, and MIG/TIG welding with a meticulous, organized approach and an artistic eye that drives his ambition to design functional art installations for future manufacturing plants.
info.cultural_background: Nicholas was raised in Fayette, Alabama, a tight‑knit Southern community where family, church, and local traditions are central. He grew up attending Methodist services, participating in community events such as high school football games, church potlucks, and county fairs. Southern hospitality, a love for comfort foods like fried chicken, collard greens, and pecan pie, and an appreciation for blues, country, and Southern rock music shaped his upbringing. While his roots are firmly Southern, exposure to college courses and a diverse peer group has broadened his perspective, fostering openness to varied cultures, artistic expressions, and unconventional ideas.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Nicholas enjoys playing electric guitar, painting landscapes and urban scenes with acrylic and watercolor, and experimenting with digital art. He regularly joins local pickup basketball games and participates in a community theater group, often helping with set design. Weekend hikes in the Talladega National Forest, car restoration projects with friends, and visits to art museums and galleries in Birmingham satisfy his love for the outdoors and culture. He also follows indie film festivals, listens to tech and science podcasts, and attends maker meetups to explore new DIY projects.
info.sports_persona: Nicholas Foley routinely joins pickup basketball games at the local community center, cheering on the Atlanta Hawks while also following the Birmingham Barons baseball team and hiking the Talladega National Forest in the summer, treating each hike as both cardio and a source of creative inspiration.
info.arts_persona: Nicholas Foley blends traditional and digital creativity, painting acrylic landscapes inspired by Monet’s light, crafting set pieces for community theater, and experimenting with Adobe Photoshop to produce surreal digital collages reminiscent of Bee Bee Bee's hyperrealism.
info.travel_persona: Nicholas Foley favors weekend road trips to nearby natural spots like the Talladega National Forest and cultural stops such as the Detroit Institute of Arts, while dreaming of a spring backpacking adventure through the national parks of Utah and a future art‑focused pilgrimage to Florence, planning each outing with a mix of spontaneity and a detailed spreadsheet.
info.culinary_persona: Nicholas Foley enjoys cooking comfort food like shrimp and grits and smoked chicken wings, seasoning dishes with smoked paprika, fresh basil, and a dash of hot sauce, while also experimenting with Asian ramen broth recipes, often ordering craft beer to pair with their meals.

info.persona: Patricia Allen is a detail‑driven metal fabricator turned sculptor whose competitive edge and artistic curiosity are tempered by bouts of anxiety, and they cherish solitary creative rituals.
info.professional_persona: Patricia Allen, a 38‑year‑old sheet‑metal fabricator with a decade of experience in MIG/TIG welding, CNC machining, blueprint reading, and OSHA compliance, balances meticulous project coordination with an artist’s eye; they apply their critical, competitive nature to mentor junior workers while channeling emotional reactivity into daring, abstract metal sculptures that blend technical precision with creative expression.
info.cultural_background: Patricia grew up in a working-class family in the Charleston region of South Carolina. Her cultural background reflects Southern traditions, including a strong sense of community, appreciation for regional cuisine, and exposure to the rich musical heritage of Charleston’s jazz and blues scenes. As a white American in the South, she was raised with Methodist influences and values such as self-reliance and personal responsibility. Her professional life in the sheet-metal trade aligns with the region’s blue-collar labor culture, while her personal curiosity and love of art bring a broader, eclectic dimension to her Southern roots.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Patricia enjoys exploring local art galleries and museums, where she draws inspiration for her own metal sculpture projects. In her spare time she designs and welds small decorative pieces, such as abstract wall art and functional furniture. She reads contemporary fiction and philosophy, listens to indie and blues music, and takes solitary walks along the Charleston waterfront. She also experiments with Southern cooking, trying new recipes on weekends, and occasionally attends small group workshops on woodworking or digital design to broaden her creative skills.
info.sports_persona: Patricia Allen, a fan of the Charleston Battery soccer team and a regular at the local paddle‑boarding club on the Cooper River, also enjoys weekly pickleball matches at the community center, using these low‑impact activities to offset the physical demands of metal fabrication while satisfying their competitive drive.
info.arts_persona: Patricia Allen, an avid visitor to the Gibbes Museum of Art and the Halsey Institute, draws creative fuel from sculptors like Richard Serra and blues guitarist Gary Clark Jr., and they curate a personal vinyl collection of indie and blues records that echo in their studio as they weld abstract wall pieces.
info.travel_persona: Patricia Allen, preferring solitary or small‑group road trips, has explored Asheville’s craft breweries, Savannah’s historic districts, and dreams of a summer study in Barcelona’s metalworking workshops, yet they balance this wanderlust with careful budgeting and occasional family obligations.
info.culinary_persona: Patricia Allen, an enthusiastic experimenter in Southern cuisine, often prepares shrimp‑and‑grits with smoked paprika, collard greens tossed in apple cider vinegar, and hand‑crafted biscuits, though they sometimes over‑salt dishes when stressed, turning cooking into both a creative outlet and a source of anxiety.
